title: Supernatural (American TV series)
wiki_lead:
Supernatural is an American dark fantasy television series created by Eric Kripke that ran for 15 seasons. It premiered on The WB on September 13, 2005, moved to The CW in 2006, and ended on November 19, 2020. Starring Jared Padalecki and Jensen Ackles, the show follows brothers Sam and Dean Winchester, who hunt ghosts, monsters, and other supernatural beings. Throughout the series, they battle angels and demons while trying to save the world and prevent the Apocalypse. Guest actors Misha Collins, Mark A. Sheppard, and Mark Pellegrino were promoted to series regulars.
The project originated from Kripke's idea of a cross-country road trip and was approved by Warner Bros. It ran for four showrunner periods: Kripke (seasons 1–5), Sera Gamble (seasons 6–7), Jeremy Carver (seasons 8–11), and the duo of Andrew Dabb and Robert Singer (seasons 12–15). The writing is based on a monster-of-the-week concept and incorporates brotherly codependency, Americana, family psychology, Judeo-Christian mythology, and self-referential humor. Production was based in Vancouver, British Columbia, with chiaroscuro cinematography by Serge Ladouceur and an in-house visual effects department to save on costs. The soundtrack combines original music by Jay Gruska and Christopher Lennertz with classic rock songs, including "Carry On Wayward Son" by Kansas.
Most episodes had an audience of over a million viewers in the United States, peaking at 5.82 million. It was the longest-running series on The CW and the longest-running fantasy series in American television history. The complete 15-season series was released on DVD and Blu-ray on May 25, 2021. Critical reception of the show was mixed to positive; critics praised the on-screen chemistry of Padalecki and Ackles and called the first five seasons its peak. Other reviewers criticized the repetitive storylines and confusing plots of later seasons. Supernatural was nominated for three Primetime Emmy Awards and won nine People's Choice Awards. The series developed a large fan base that regularly attends conventions. Other media include novel and comic adaptations as well as spin-offs such as The Winchesters (2022–2023).

Premise


Plot

In their childhood, Sam and Dean Winchester lose their mother Mary to a mysterious supernatural creature, prompting their father John to raise them as hunters to track it. The first three seasons focus on the brothers' lives as hunters on the road, beginning with their search for their missing father. Sam is studying at Stanford University with his girlfriend Jessica until she is killed in the same way as his mother. He then leaves school and joins Dean; they travel around the United States hunting monsters, ghosts, demons, and other supernatural beings which are often drawn from folklore and urban legends.
John trades his life to keep Dean alive at the beginning of the second season. The brothers find that the yellow-eyed demon Azazel was responsible for killing Mary and Jessica and forcing Sam to consume demon blood as a baby. After Sam is killed, Dean makes a deal with a crossroads demon to bring Sam back, trading his soul for Sam's resurrection and leaving himself with only one year to live. The brothers then destroy Azazel. Dean's deal expires at the end of the third season and he is dragged to Hell by hellhounds, but the angel Castiel resurrects him at the beginning of the fourth season. Developing empathy for humanity, Castiel turns against Heaven and joins the Winchesters to prevent the coming Apocalypse. Manipulated by the demon Ruby and the demon blood, Sam kills Lilith, inadvertently releasing the fallen archangel Lucifer from his imprisonment in Hell.
By the fifth season, Sam and Dean are destined to be the "vessels" for Lucifer and the archangel Michael, respectively, in a final world-ending battle. Sam breaks free of the possession and imprisons Michael and Lucifer by throwing himself into Lucifer's Cage and is later resurrected by Castiel. In the sixth season, Castiel and the demon Crowley find a way to reach Purgatory to keep the archangel Raphael from restarting the Apocalypse, which unleashes monsters called Leviathans. During the seventh season, the brothers battle the Leviathans and their leader Dick Roman to destroy them and prevent the use of human beings as a food source. Following Roman's demise, Dean is trapped in Purgatory for a year before returning to assist Sam in closing the Gates of Hell through a series of trials in the eighth season.
The angel Metatron creates a spell that expels all angels from Heaven to Earth. Tricked out of his grace and betrayed, Castiel becomes a regular human and struggles to survive during the ninth season. Dean tricks Sam, who is dying, into allowing an angel to possess his body to save him, which causes conflict between the brothers and leads Dean to accept the Mark of Cain to gain enough power to kill the demon Abaddon. This Mark also causes violence in Dean, making him be reborn as a demon after his death. When Sam and Rowena MacLeod try to cast a spell from the Book of the Damned to remove the Mark, they release Amara, God's sister and the entity known as the Darkness.
God is revealed to be the prophet and novelist Chuck Shurley. In the eleventh season, Chuck teams up with others to try to conquer Amara, but they ultimately resolve their sibling conflict. Amara resurrects Mary Winchester to thank the brothers. In the twelfth season, Lucifer impregnates a human woman and fathers a Nephilim named Jack Kline. Despite fearing Jack is dangerous, the brothers adopt him along with Castiel; however, Jack opens a dimensional portal to an apocalyptic alternate universe and releases an evil alternate Michael. Dean offers to be Michael's vessel to destroy Lucifer and rescue Jack and Sam. Jack expends his remaining power to eliminate Michael, but loses his soul and accidentally kills Mary.
Chuck resurfaces and demands the brothers kill Jack. Once aware that Chuck has been controlling their lives for his own entertainment, Sam and Dean defy him, angering Chuck. The fifteenth and final season chronicles the Winchesters' climactic rebellion against God, in which Castiel gives his life to save Dean from Death and is thrown into the Empty, where angels and demons reside after death. Jack absorbs Chuck's power, which lets the brothers reclaim their free will. Dean dies on a routine hunting trip; Sam lives to old age, and the brothers are finally reunited in Heaven.


Characters

The premise of Supernatural is the quest of two brothers, Sam (Jared Padalecki) and Dean Winchester (Jensen Ackles), to hunt supernatural creatures. Sam is portrayed as rebellious and intelligent, wishing for a normal life; Dean is more of an action man, exhibiting a protective nature, loyalty, and dedication to the family business. Their motto is "saving people, hunting things, the family business".
The series has many recurring characters. John Winchester (Jeffrey Dean Morgan) is the father who trains the brothers to hunt demons. After his death, veteran hunter Bobby Singer (Jim Beaver) becomes a surrogate father for the brothers and mentors them. The third season is the only one with Katie Cassidy (as Ruby) and Lauren Cohan (as the thief Bela Talbot) in the main cast. After Cassidy's departure, Ruby was played by Genevieve Cortese in the fourth season.
In the fourth season, Misha Collins joined the cast as Castiel; scholar Louisa Ellen Stein wrote that his introduction marked a conceptual transition for the series. Despite the former angel Anna Milton's description of angels as emotionless, many of them can be influenced, including Castiel, who develops empathy for humans, rebels against Heaven to side with Sam and Dean, and becomes part of Team Free Will. Castiel's popularity resulted in Collins's promotion to series regular, and he was part of the main cast for seasons 5–6 and 9–15. During the brothers' quest, they are assisted by Ellen (Samantha Ferris) and her daughter Jo Harvelle (Alona Tal), hacker Charlie Bradbury (Felicia Day), prophet Kevin Tran (Osric Chau), and Rowena MacLeod (Ruth Connell). In seasons 13–15, Alexander Calvert joined the main cast as Jack Kline, a powerful young Nephilim who is adopted and protected by the Winchesters and Castiel.
Mark A. Sheppard portrayed Crowley as a series regular in seasons 10–12. Introduced in the fifth season, Crowley is a clever crossroads demon who maneuvers into the position of King of Hell and plays both sides against the middle to serve his own interests. After joining the series in the fifth season, Mark Pellegrino played Lucifer's primary vessel across multiple seasons and eventually was promoted to the main cast for seasons 12–14. Antagonists who turn into allies include the demon Meg Masters (Nicki Aycox and Rachel Miner) and the archangel Gabriel, also known as the Trickster (Richard Speight Jr.). Other notable villains include Azazel (Fredric Lehne), Lilith (Katherine Boecher), Dick Roman (James Patrick Stuart), Metatron (Curtis Armstrong), Abaddon (Alaina Huffman), Amara the Darkness (Emily Swallow), and Chuck Shurley (Rob Benedict), who turns out to be God.


Themes

Supernatural blends the genres of dark fantasy, action-adventure, and melodrama, with elements of soap opera, Western, road movie, slapstick comedy, Gothic horror, splatter, and slasher. Most episodes begin with a weekly mystery case in which a creature stalks and kills a random minor character. Sam and Dean travel around the US in a 1967 Chevrolet Impala, which they consider their "real home", where they share personal struggles, bicker, and exchange banter such as "bitch" and "jerk". The brothers find supernatural events by searching newspapers and websites. To conduct interrogations and bypass local police, they use fake IDs and impersonate officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or other law enforcement agencies. Sam usually handles the research using libraries and the internet.
On a typical hunt, the brothers investigate an unexplained death or supernatural threat. They determine who or what the culprit is, track it down, and kill it. Their father's journal, a reference book, helps them through danger; scholar Rebecca Stone Gordon characterized it as a deus ex machina. They are often assisted by Bobby, Castiel, Crowley, and other allies. The tools they commonly use to combat supernatural entities include salting (to ward off ghosts or demons) and burning (to wipe out a spirit's corpse); specific objects, folk remedies, or incantations; and special weapons such as the Word of God tablets, the Colt revolver, flasks of holy water, wooden stakes, Ruby's knife, silver blades, and silver bullets. Once a case is closed, the brothers move on until they stumble upon another.
The brotherly love between Sam and Dean is central to the series; the angel Zachariah refers to their relationship as "psychotically, irrationally, and erotically" codependent. The brothers have a propensity for engaging in immoral and unethical activities to keep each other safe, and suffer psychological distress if they fail to do so. Their willingness to give up their lives to save each other results in a cycle of sacrifice, death, resurrection, and torture. The show deals with the idea of found family, embodied by Bobby's quote "Family don't end with blood", and suggests that family has more to do with personal choice and mutual acceptance than with biology. The Winchester brothers introduce non-humans such as the angel Castiel and the Nephilim Jack into their family. The concept of family extends to a cosmic level: Lucifer's war with the other angels is one between brothers; God's conflict with his sister, the Darkness, is a family dispute.

grok_lead: Supernatural is an American dark fantasy drama television series created by Eric Kripke, starring Jared Padalecki as Sam Winchester and Jensen Ackles as Dean Winchester, two brothers who travel across the United States in a 1967 Chevrolet Impala, hunting demons, ghosts, monsters, and other supernatural entities while unraveling family secrets and apocalyptic threats. The series blends genres of horror, action-adventure, mystery, and drama, featuring a mix of standalone "monster-of-the-week" episodes and overarching mythological arcs involving angels, gods, and cosmic battles. Premiering on September 13, 2005, on The WB network, Supernatural transitioned to The CW after the networks' merger and ran for 15 seasons, totaling 327 episodes until its series finale on November 19, 2020. Originally envisioned by Kripke as a five-season story, the show's popularity led to its extension, evolving from episodic hunts to complex narratives exploring themes of family, destiny, and redemption. The series introduced recurring characters like the angel Castiel, played by Misha Collins, who joins the brothers in later seasons, adding layers to its supernatural lore. Produced by Warner Bros. Television, Supernatural developed a devoted fanbase, often called the "SPN Family," known for conventions and fan campaigns that contributed to its longevity. It received three Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including for Outstanding Sound Editing in 2006 and 2008, and Outstanding Music Composition in 2006, and earned two wins at the Saturn Awards, for Best Network Television Series in 2006 and Best Television Series in 2010.
